# dsh-next-hint

> When a turn ends, the composer suggests the next message by itself.
> **Tab accepts, nothing is ev

urn ends, the composer suggests the next message by itself.
> **Tab accepts, nothing is ever sent.**

A DeepSeek Harness plugin that brings
Claude Code–style prompt suggestions to DSH — as **ghost text*

* inside your own
composer: visible, undoable, and never on the return key.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
## Why install it

- **It knows what you were doing.** One **decoupled auxiliary request** reads the
last few turns of

*this* session — the file you touched, the test that went red,
where the work stopped — instead of a

template like "continue?".
- **It never touches your Enter key.** Accepting inserts ordinary text i

nto the
draft. `Ctrl+Z` undoes it; sending stays your decision. There is no send path in
the code at

all.
- **It stays quiet.** No route, timeout, rate limit, malformed output, or a plain
"not today"

all end as **no ghost** and no error surface — at most one warn in
the log.
- **It does not ship you

r conversation anywhere.** The browser posts a
`sessionId`; the host reads the transcript inside its

own process, writes it
nowhere, logs no text, and keeps it on this machine.
## Install
**DSH Desktop**: Settings → Plugins → add a git package
[代码示例省略，未执行]

The desktop profile is owned by the app — `dsh plugin --profile desktop …` is refused by the CLI.
Fo
r a self-managed profile such as `web`:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Restart the app once — plugins join the roster at boot.

> **Updating:** the plugin page's update check only compares npm-registry sources; a
> `github:` ins

tall is skipped and always reads as "latest". For a GitHub install use
> one of these, then restart

the app:
>
[代码示例省略，未执行]

>
> or uninstall it on the plugin page and add `github:xiaoshenming/dsh-next-hint#main`
> again. To
use the in-app update button, install the plugin from npm once it is published.
## What you get
| Moment | What happens |
| A turn settles, draft is empty | One grey line at the composer's first line, `Tab accept` on the r

ight |
| `Tab` with focus in the composer | The sentence lands in the draft, caret at its end, **not

sent** |
| You start typing | The ghost disappears |
| You switch sessions | The ghost is dropped |
| Two declines / timeout / no route | Nothing at all — the correct outcome |

A model that answers "nothing to suggest" is asked once more with a stricter
instruction before the
plugin gives up: one refusal never blanks the whole turn.

Tab only fires when no candidate menu owns it: with the `/` or `@` menu open,
Tab still belongs to t

fires when no candidate menu owns it: with the `/` or `@` menu open,
Tab still belongs to the menu.
## Configuration
Settings → Plugins → dsh-next-hint. Every key has a default; nothing is required.
| Key | Default | Meaning |

| `enabled` | `true` | Master switch |
| `provider` / `model` | empty | Empty follows the session's

last route; set both or neither |
| `locale` | `auto` | Language of the suggestion |
| `maxTurns` |

`3` | Exchanges sampled |
| `maxInputBytes` | `8000` | Input budget for the auxiliary request |
| `m

axOutputTokens` | `128` | Output token cap |
| `maxHintChars` | `48` | Hint length cap; a paragraph

is dropped, a long sentence truncated |
| `timeoutMs` | `15000` | Per-call timeout |
| `perSessionCo
oldownMs` | `0` | Per-session cooldown; default suggests every turn |
## How it works

A dual-face cordis plugin, the same shape as
dsh-session-surgeon:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Deliberate choices:

- **Decide in the browser, generate in the host.** Only the browser knows whether
the draft is empty

, whether you are typing, and which session is on screen;
asking the host to guess gets it wrong twi

ce.
- **One request/response.** No SSE, no long-lived connections, no server-side
cache. Cancelling

is `AbortController.abort()`.
- **Official slot, own pixels.** The component mounts in
`conversation

.composer.dock`; the ghost node is ours because the host exposes
no inline-hint write path. Unmounti

ng removes the node, the listeners, and the
in-flight request.
- **The auxiliary call follows the se

ssion-title recipe**: its own system
instruction, its own timeout, the cheapest reasoning level, and

a failure that
cannot touch the main conversation.
## Related work
Four same-kind plugins now exist, plus one complementary tool; **prefer one same-kind**:

- **This plugin**: official dock slot and a stateless host route; Tab accepts, the offer is
dropped

on a session switch.
- Composer predictions (`dsh-composer-prediction`):
same idea; overlay slot, pe

r-session cache, Esc, settings page. From 0.7.7 it detects this
plugin and pauses itself (this plugi

n wins).
- Composer Predictions (`dsh-composer-predictions`):
same idea plus draft continuation; Alt

+↑/↓ candidate cycling, Esc, owner admission; needs
DSH ≥0.2.1-rc.3.
- Reply Suggestions (`dsh-reply

-suggestions`):
same idea; Enter-to-fill, Esc, usage/cost stats; built for rc.2.
- **Complementary**

: `dsh-input-assist`
completes *the sentence you are typing* and checks typos; this plugin suggests

*the next
message after a turn*. The only overlap is an idle empty composer — if you see two ghosts
there, turn one of them off.
## Compatibility
- Measured on **DSH Desktop `0.2.1-rc.2` (Windows)** and the same version's **web profile (macOS)**.

The host half needs
`ctx.llm`, `ctx.sessions`, and `ctx.webServer.register`; the browser half needs

the `conversation.composer.dock` slot and the composer input facade.
- Re-checked against the insta

lled **`0.2.2-rc.1`** build by scanning its `app.asar`:
every seam above still exists, and `conversa

tion.composer.dock` is a `list` slot, so it
coexists with other composer plugins. A real GUI run on

rc.1 is still pending.
- Still `0.x`: if upstream moves those seams, the ghost breaks first. Its pos

ition
relies on the editor's `[data-input-scroll]` structure; a missing anchor means
no ghost, silen

tly.
- Requests from outside loopback are refused by the route.
- If DSH ships this natively, this p

lugin can be disabled cleanly — nothing here
assumes it is the only writer of the composer.
